topic.readerProblem: A founder or marketer facing ChatGPT, Google's AI features, Gemini, Perplexity and Claude needs to know which engine to work on first and how to justify that order with their own data rather than a generic ranking.
topic.connection: AEOeye's audits test the same buyer questions across five AI engines; the page turns that into a decision method, uses our crawler access study and recommendation benchmark with their limits, and points to the free audit and $29 full report as one way to run the comparison.

assessment: The page gives a default order (Google, then ChatGPT) with the reason, rules for when to override it, a table of what each vendor documents and what to do first, the shared foundation, and a five-step method for deciding with the reader's own buyer questions. It rests on Google, OpenAI, Perplexity and Anthropic documentation, Pew Research Center's February 2026 chatbot-use survey, SparkToro's answer-variability study, and AEOeye's crawler study and audit records, each with sample size and caveat. It deliberately does not rank engines from AEOeye's benchmark, does not state which third-party indexes feed ChatGPT search (OpenAI's help page could not be fetched), and does not claim any usage figure for Perplexity.

sources.supports: Google's generative AI features (AI Overviews, AI Mode) are rooted in core Search ranking and quality systems and retrieve pages from the Search index.
No additional requirements, special schema or AI text files needed to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode.
Google-Extended governs use for training Gemini models and for grounding in Gemini Apps, and does not affect Search inclusion or ranking.
OAI-SearchBot surfaces websites in ChatGPT's search features; opted-out sites are not shown in ChatGPT search answers.
PerplexityBot surfaces and links websites in Perplexity search results; a web application firewall may need explicit allowlisting.
Claude-SearchBot navigates the web to improve search result quality; disabling it may reduce visibility in user search results.
Pew survey of US adults, Feb 17-23, 2026 (published June 17, 2026): share who ever use ChatGPT 44%, Gemini 24%, Copilot 17%, Meta AI 14%, Grok 8%, Claude 6%; Perplexity not included.

600 volunteers ran 12 prompts across ChatGPT, Claude and Google AI 2,961 times; under a 1 in 100 chance ChatGPT or Google's AI give the same brand list in any two responses (published January 28, 2026).
